critic: LEAD (independent critic, checked by a second agent)
verdict:
A real step up on the round-6 notes that were taken. The scale close-up is a proper object shot now. There are no slivers of Dawn, the plate rim sits inside the frame and the duffel's top shows its folds (graded about 60). The display face is the brightest area in the frame (median 190 graded), but three small highlights match or beat it: the post just under the display head (200-208), the case's zip pullers (up to 223) and the plate's front rim (175-188). The shoulder booklet is whole and well inside the frame, with real contact shadows under the pads. The wide's overhead sign is dimmed to about 54, and the lower-left floor is dark enough to carry type (median 22-23 under it). As the film's first fifteen seconds (0:00-0:15 in SCRIPT_V2's direction), the sequence still falls short of fern, for four reasons.

1. Shot 1's subject is the readout, which says OVERWEIGHT in the existing composite. It is small (178 x 75-78 px, 9% of the frame width) and sits behind the focus plane: focus is on the duffel at 2.29 m, the display is at 2.77-2.92 m, f/2.8. The composite then blurs the type with a 2.2 px Gaussian, which is softer than the panel's own edges (a sigma of about 1.2-1.3 px).
2. In shot 2 the hand still stands on its fingertips at the booklet's trailing edge. The knuckles are high, the fingers are gapped and the thumb is hidden. The hand is still hotter than the face: the lit fingers measure a median of about 151-160 and a p95 of 185-186, against about 149-151 and 163-165 on the face. The frame's brightest pixel, 191, is a fingertip. The booklet is a mid-grey tile with no page edge, so it reads as a coaster or a phone rather than a passport. The beat it covers is 'she pays it', and a passport alone says check-in, not payment.
3. In shot 3 a queue stanchion (q1_1) comes straight down into the '4' of '2014', and its base sits behind the '1' and '4' at the baseline. A second post (q1_0) stands about 50 px above the '20'.
4. The wide, which carries the title, exists only at 1280 px and is upscaled into the 1920 super. It follows a 1920 master for shot 1.

Two problems remain in the reverse. The hair shell still shows hard stepped bands above the near ear: it is already smooth-shaded and subdivided, so the bands are in its shape. And a pale knob sticks out of her frame-right jaw at mouth level.
answers:
PINS (verified). The four pins in scale.corners.json match the visible face. I found each edge as the halfway point between the face and the bezel (raw 232 against about 17-19). Rows y 180/212/245 glow over x 1170-1352, 1165-1348 and 1161-1343. The pins interpolate to 1172.6-1349.8, 1167.9-1345.3 and 1163.0-1340.6. Columns x 1180/1260/1340 glow over y 173/171/169 to 251, and the pins give 175.3/173.3/171.3 to about 249. So the glow reaches 2-3.5 px past the pins on every side. That is the 1.5 mm disp_bleed hairline at x ±0.1215 and z ±0.0465 plus the defocus, which is what you would expect if the pins track the scale_display face itself. They are correct.

The existing composite (gfx/scale.html through gfx/doc_composite.py, out/gfx/scale_overweight.mp4) already uses the near-white face (raw 232, graded 190) the right way: it multiplies dark LCD segments into the plate's own glow, so the face needs no emission cut. Its blur is too strong, though. tex_blur_px is 2.2 (a Gaussian sigma), while the panel's own top and left edges rise from 10% to 90% over 3.0-3.5 px, a sigma of about 1.2-1.3 px. So the word is softer than the glass it sits on, and about 1.2 would match the current plate. On a 178 px face the word spans about 150 px: about 15 px a letter and 25 px of cap height. That is readable on a desktop at 1080 but not on a phone, and it is the film's first word.

1) Do the bags work as shot 1? As a picture of two bags on a weighing unit with a readout, yes, and it is the cleanest this camera has been. The duffel's top reads as fabric (graded about 60, with folds and straps), the case shows its zips and pocket, and both sit with contact on the plate. They are still silhouettes, though: the duffel front is 24-25, its ends 18-20 and the case front 27. Near-black voids fill about 40% of the width. The counter-end slab at x 0-280 has a median of 16, and the floor and wall at x 1450-1900 a median of 13.

The display post's specular highlight is the hottest form in the frame. It measures 200-208 graded over the 150 px just under the display head (y 335-490), brighter than the face itself (median 190, max 198), then fades to 40-55 down the post. The case's zip pullers peak at 223, and the plate's front rim runs about 600 px at 175-188. So at pixel level the readout is not the brightest thing.

The bigger issue is that the shot's subject at 0:00 is the readout ('The bags are overweight'), and it sits in the soft zone. The focus is on focus_duffel at 2.29 m, with the display 0.5-0.6 m behind it at f/2.8. The duffel focus is by design: it is the extra bag, and SCRIPT_V2's direction is 'the display settles; the duffel on the plate'. So the cure is more depth of field, not moving the focus off the bag.

2) Does the passport gesture work as shot 2? Only half.

Fixed: the booklet is wholly in frame, its near edge about 65-70 px above the bottom of the frame. There are contact shadows under the pads, and the steel nosing is well inside the frame.

Not fixed: the hand. The fingertips sit on the booklet's trailing (Dawn-side) edge, the knuckles stand high, there are visible gaps between the fingers and the thumb is hidden. At 3x zoom it still reads as fingertips pinning or tapping, not a flat hand sliding something across. The hand is also still the hottest skin. The lit fingers measure a median of about 151-160 and a p95 of 185-186, against about 149-151 and 163-165 on the face at the same thresholds. The frame's maximum, 191, is on a fingertip at (591, 607), so the eye goes to the hand before her face.

The booklet itself reads as a grey tile. Its cover is graded about 97 on a ledge of about 78-80. The pages are modelled 3 mm smaller than the covers (0.125 x 0.087 against 0.128 x 0.090), so the cream page block is recessed into shadow and never shows. The column profiles go straight from the cover (89-105) to a shadow line (34-45).

Little in the reverse says 'check-in counter' either. There are soft queue posts behind her, but no monitor, no bag-tag printer and no bag belt. The waist-high ledge and the framing read as a desk or table, close to the inspection bench (Dawn standing across from the officers) that follows at 0:20.

The voice over this shot (0:04-0:09) is 'Only slightly. There's a small fee, and she pays it without a second thought.' A passport says 'checks in'; a card or cash says 'pays'. SCRIPT_V2's direction asks for 'her hand slides the booklet across', so a card laid on the passport keeps that action and adds the payment.

3) Does the dark title position work in shot 3? The darkness is real. I measured the background of the 1920 super under the type at a median of 22-23, p90 27 and p99 32, so your numbers stand. With the type at 231 (bounding box x 142-321, y 822-952), legibility is excellent, and title left against action right balances the frame.

But the position collides with the set. Projected with the wide camera, stanchion q1_1 at world (-2.6, -3.3) has its shaft at x 275-286, running from y 639 down to its base at (286, 853). The post runs into the '4' of '2014', and its base sits behind the '1' and the '4' at the type's baseline. Stanchion q1_0 at (-4.6, -3.3) has its base at (195, 766), about 50 px above the '20'. The date looks planted on queue posts.

Separately, the wide is rendered at 1280x720 and upscaled to 1920 for the super: the super's plate matches the current wide.jpg, upscaled, within 0.42/255 on average. So the title shot is softer than the 1920 scale master that opens the film.

4) Do they work as three successive cuts? The grammar works: object detail, then the person's hand and face, then the establishing shot with the date, which is the right reverse-order cold open. The axis holds: Dawn is screen-left and the agent screen-right in both the shoulder and the wide. The bags keep their arrangement from scale to wide (duffel in front, case behind, display at the plate's back corner), and the wide shows the display glowing, so the geography ties up. Exposure is steady: frame means of 24, 34 and 33, medians of 19, 25 and 27.

What breaks the sequence are the three faults above. The hook word is small and soft, the 'pays' beat shows a passport tapped by fingertips under a hand brighter than the face, and the date lands on a post. Fix those three and the sequence cuts cleanly.

PROFILE (not in this batch, for context): profile.jpg dates from 06:54, before commit 32023cc (08:45). That commit set dawn-suitcase to sat 0.35 / val 0.5 and the monitor glow from 3.0 to 1.8. The frame still shows the old state: the case's display-side face is lighter blue-grey than the duffel, and the monitor is the largest bright surface between the two people. It needs a re-render, not a new change.

fixes.problem: The hand stands on its fingertips at the booklet's trailing edge: the knuckles are high, the fingers gapped and the thumb hidden. It reads as pinning or tapping, not sliding a booklet across.
fixes.fix:
Booklet: in pose_cast, set piece.location.y = hand['pad'].y + 0.012 instead of + 0.030, so the booklet sits further under the hand and the pads land 30-35 mm in from its trailing edge. Check that 20-30 mm of ledge stays behind it.

Finger bends: in rest_hand, cap the bend at 10.0 for the passing hand only. The clamp at line 1227 (max(3.0, min(27.0, ...))) is shared with the agent's typing hands, so leave it at 27.0 when not passing. In the passing branch, set the finger joints to (bend, 2, 2).

palm_drop: leave it near its current -0.002. The solver aims the palm's lowest point at finger_z - palm_drop, so -0.002 already puts the heel about 8 mm above the ledge. A positive value would push the heel into the ledge.

Finger gaps: close them through articulate_hand's fourth value (spread in the palm plane, positive toward the thumb). Setting rotation_euler.z will not work, because articulate_hand resets it. Try f_index (bend, 2, 2, -3), f_middle (bend, 2, 2, 0), f_ring (bend, 2, 2, 2) and f_pinky (bend, 2, 2, 4), and aim for neighbouring fingertips 1-3 mm apart on the posed mesh.

Thumb: open it out to lie along the booklet's frame-left (inner) edge, visible to the camera. Use thumb (10, 25, 5, -5) and let the existing basal-joint loop settle it.

Check at 3x zoom: each finger's middle phalanx within 10 mm of the cover, the knuckles no more than about 15 mm above it, and the fingers reading as one flat blade.

fixes.problem: In the 1920 super, stanchion q1_1 (-2.6, -3.3) comes down into the '4' of '2014' (shaft x 275-286, base at 286,853, behind the '1' and '4'). q1_0's base (195,766) sits about 50 px above the '20'. The title looks planted on queue posts.
fixes.fix:
In queue(), change the front row from (-3.3, [-4.6, -2.6, -0.3]) to (-3.0, [-5.4, -1.4, -0.3]). Projected with the wide camera, the bases land at (221,733), (440,911) and (548,998) in 1920 px. That leaves about 80 px of clear floor above the type and about 75 px between the type's right edge and the nearest base edge. The belt between the first two posts runs from (213,584) to (432,686), above the type.

Move q0_0 to x -5.4 as well, and rebuild q_link0 from (-5.4, -2.1) to (-5.4, -3.0). The lane narrows from 1.2 m to 0.9 m and the front belt becomes 4.0 m long, both within normal airport practice.

Re-measure the type box (x 130-340, y 800-970): it should hold no post pixels and have a median of 25 or less. These posts also stand behind Dawn in the shoulder and the profile, so re-check those backgrounds.

fixes.problem: The hand is still brighter than the face. The lit fingers measure a median of about 151-160 and a p95 of 185-186, against about 149-151 and 163-165 on the face, and the frame's brightest pixel (191) is a fingertip. The eye lands on the hand before Dawn.
fixes.fix:
The hand flag at z 1.55 is not enough. Add a second unseen flag, 'hand flag2', 0.14 x 0.10 m, about 0.35 m above the ledge. Centre it over her hand using hand['palm'] from rest_hand (the wrist target is at x DAWN[0]-0.20 = 0.30). Turn every visibility flag off except shadow, as the existing flags are set up.

If the flag cannot reach the target without darkening her forearm, light-link island and down_front away from the hand instead, by moving Dawn's left-hand vertices into their own armature-deformed object. Do not darken the hand's material: the cast keeps one stone finish (DECISIONS).

Target: lit fingers at a median of 125-135 graded and a p95 of at most 150, with the face unchanged at about 150.

fixes.problem: The hook readout, the shot's subject at 0:00, is soft and small. The focus is on the duffel at 2.29 m and the display is at 2.77-2.92 m, at f/2.8 (a 3.1-3.9 px circle of confusion). The composite then blurs the type a further 2.2 px (tex_blur_px). The face is 178 x 75-78 px, so OVERWEIGHT spans only about 150 px.
fixes.fix:
Keep the duffel sharp: it is the extra bag and is focused by design. Gain depth of field instead. Put a focus empty at 2.55 m along the camera axis, between the duffel and the display, and set fstop to 5.6. The duffel's centre (2.29 m) and the display (2.77-2.92 m) then both land at about 0.6-1.0 px of blur at 46 mm, and the dark background still falls away. Re-render, re-export scale.corners.json (frame_metadata writes focus_m and fstop), and lower tex_blur_px in gfx/shots/scale_overweight.json to about 0.5.

If the plate is not re-rendered, still lower tex_blur_px from 2.2 to about 1.2. The panel's own edges rise from 10% to 90% over 3.0-3.5 px (a Gaussian sigma of about 1.2-1.3 px), so 2.2 makes the word softer than the glass.

Do not cut the display's emission. The composite multiplies dark LCD segments into the lit face, and the bright face is what gives them their contrast.

For size: the composite already pushes in from 1.0 to 1.035 (the zoom in scale_overweight.json). A real 46-to-56 mm push in Blender would end with the display about 217 px wide, but it needs the plate rendered as a sequence with corners per frame. Weigh that against a stronger push in the composite from a higher-resolution still.

fixes.problem: The title shot is rendered at 1280x720 and upscaled to 1920 for the super, so it is softer than the 1920 scale master it follows by two cuts.
fixes.fix: Add final_res=(1920, 1080) to CAMERAS['wide'], as on scale, re-render (together with the queue move), and rebuild out/gfx/cut/wide_2014.png from the native plate.

fixes.problem: The booklet reads as a grey tile or a coaster. The page block is inset 1.5 mm into shadow and never shows, and nothing in the frame says 'pays', the beat this shot covers.
fixes.fix:
In desk(), make the pages 0.127 x 0.089, 0.5 mm inside the covers. The cream page edge, about 3.6 mm thick, then shows as a band about 4 px tall on the near side (about 1.2 px per mm at this distance).

If a wedge of pages is also wanted, hinge the 'front' cover open about 1 deg about its spine edge. That gives a gap of about 2 mm (2-3 px) at the fore-edge. Do not use 3-4 deg: that opens 7-9 mm, which reads as an open cover.

Then lay a plain payment card on top of the passport, under her index and middle fingers: 0.0856 x 0.054 x 0.0008, corner bevel 0.003, matte dark grey (albedo about 0.05), nothing printed, standing about 15 mm proud of the booklet's agent-side edge. The gesture then reads 'hands over passport and card: pays', and the direction's 'slides the booklet across' still holds.

fixes.problem: About 40% of the width is near-black dead space: the left counter slab has a median of 16, the right floor and wall a median of 13. The display post's specular highlight is 200-208 graded over the 150 px just under the head, brighter than the display face (median 190). The case's zip pullers (up to 223) and the plate's front rim (175-188 along about 600 px) also compete. The bags are still silhouettes: duffel front 24-25, ends 18-20, case front 27.
fixes.fix:
Change the roughness of steel_v (brushed steel vertical, used only on the post) from (0.2, 0.34) to (0.45, 0.55), so the highlight stays under about 90 graded. Swapping the post to m['satin'] would not help, because satin (0.24, 0.32) is no rougher. Check that the zip pullers and the plate's front rim also stay under the display face.

Add an unseen cool area light, 0.4 x 0.3 m, about 0.6 m frame-right of the duffel's right end at plate height, at 8-12 W. Light-link it to the bags only: the children of 'extra-bag-closed' and 'dawn-suitcase', collected the way build() collects them for the display lights. The aim is for the duffel's right end and the case's right edge to reach raw 40-50, above their shadow sides, with the display still the brightest area.

fixes.problem: The hair shell still shows hard stepped bands above the near ear. A pale knob (x 478-495, y 195-228) sticks out of the frame-right jaw at mouth level and reads as a growth or a pearl earring.
fixes.fix:
The hair already has shade smooth and a level-2 Subdivision (cast._hair; people._sculpt_hair adds 'soft scalp silhouette' at levels 2), so the bands are in the shape, not faceting. The likely cause is the 'hug' shrinkwrap (nearest surface point, offset 0.0005 in _sculpt_hair). It pulls the shell onto the ear and skull ridges before 'volume' displaces along those creased normals.

Add a Smooth modifier directly after 'hug' (factor about 0.8, 10-20 repeats), or raise the hug offset to about 2-3 mm, and check above the near ear at 3x zoom. _sculpt_hair is shared by the whole cast, so re-check one other stage.

To find the knob, project the head's vertices into the shoulder camera (project() at 1280x720) and list the objects that land in that box. If it is the far ear, reduce the head turn by 3-5 deg in aim_head_iter's target, or hide the ear under the hair shell. If it is part of the bun, sink the bun further into the skull.

fixes.problem: This camera is not in the batch. profile.jpg (06:54) predates commit 32023cc, so it still shows the case's display-side face lighter blue-grey than the duffel and the monitor as the largest bright surface between the two people.
fixes.fix: The code already has both round-6 changes: dawn-suitcase at sat 0.35 and val 0.5, and the monitor glow at 1.8 (down from 3.0). Re-render the profile with the next batch so all four cameras match, and check that the case and the monitor now sit right.
